sun.name: The Sun (Sol)
sun.fact: The yellow dwarf star at the heart of our solar system. It accounts for 99.86% of all mass in the solar system, generating light and life through core nuclear fusion.

kids.title: The Mega Powerhouse!
kids.jump: Jump height: 0 inches! The gravity is 28× stronger than Earth, so you would be glued flat like toast.
kids.fact: One million Earths could fit inside the Sun! It holds 99.8% of all the stuff in our solar system.

stats.label: Spectral Class
stats.kids: Even though people call the Sun a "yellow dwarf", it is not small at all! G2V is a special star code that means it is a bright, yellow powerhouse star in the best years of its life.

stats.label: Surface Temperature
stats.sub: Surface is 55 times boiling water; core is 150,000 times hotter than boiling water (~15M°C)
stats.kids: The surface of the Sun is 5,500°C—hotter than 55 times your hot bath water! Deep inside its core, it is 150,000 times hotter than boiling water (~15 million °C)!

stats.label: Equatorial Diameter
stats.kids: The Sun is enormous! If the Sun were a huge hollow beach ball, you could fit more than one million Earths inside it like tiny glass marbles.

stats.label: Mass
stats.kids: The Sun holds 99.86% of all the matter in our whole solar system! Percent (%) means parts out of 100—if all 8 planets, moons, asteroids, and comets were 10,000 building blocks, the Sun alone would be 9,986 of them, leaving just 14 tiny blocks for everything else combined!

stats.label: Galactic Velocity
stats.kids: Our Sun zooms around the Milky Way galaxy at 220 kilometers every single second! That is over 700 times faster than a speeding bullet train.

stats.label: Distance to Earth
stats.kids: The Sun is 150 million kilometers away. Light from the Sun is the fastest traveler in the universe, but it still takes 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach your eyes on Earth!

stats.label: Rotation Period
stats.kids: The Sun is a giant spinning ball of superhot gas and plasma. Because it is not solid rock, its middle equator spins once in 25 days, but its poles take 34 days!

stats.label: Composition
stats.kids:
The percent sign (%) means parts out of 100! If you took 100 scoops of the Sun:
• H₂ (73 scoops) is Hydrogen gas: the lightest, simplest gas in the universe! It catches fire easily and acts like fuel for the Sun’s gigantic nuclear furnace.
• He (25 scoops) is Helium gas: the second-lightest gas—the very same floaty gas that makes party balloons fly up to the ceiling!
Together, H₂ and He generate all the sunshine and warmth keeping Earth alive.

mercury.name: Mercury
mercury.fact: The smallest planet — a day lasts longer than a year, with temperatures ranging from −180°C to 430°C.

kids.title: Moon-Boots Playground!
kids.jump: You can leap nearly 3× higher than on Earth! One small hop would launch you clean over your bed.
kids.fact: A year on Mercury is super fast (88 days), but one single daytime lasts longer than a whole year!

stats.label: Distance from Sun
stats.kids: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun! If you stood on Mercury, the Sun would look 3 times bigger in the sky than it does from Earth.

stats.label: Orbital Period
stats.kids: Mercury is the fastest runner in space! It zooms around the Sun in just 88 days, so you would have a birthday party every 3 months on Mercury!

stats.label: Day Length
stats.kids: Mercury spins like a sleepy top. One daytime on Mercury takes 176 Earth days—that is longer than a whole Mercury year! You would have to wait 6 months between breakfast and bedtime.

stats.label: Equatorial Radius
stats.kids: Mercury is the baby planet of our solar system—only a little bigger than our Moon. It is covered in craters from space meteorites, looking like a giant golf ball.

stats.label: Mass
stats.kids: Even though Mercury is small, it is super heavy and dense because it has a huge ball of solid iron metal inside that fills up most of the planet!

stats.label: Surface Temperature
stats.sub: Day is 4 times boiling water; night is 9 times colder than a freezer
stats.kids: Mercury has no blanket of air! During the day, it is 4 times hotter than boiling water. But at night, it plunges to −180°C, which is 9 times colder than a kitchen freezer!

stats.label: Moons & Rings
stats.sub: Mercury has no moons or natural satellites
stats.kids: Mercury has 0 moons and 0 rings! It travels so close to the Sun that the Sun’s gigantic gravity would snatch away any moon that tried to circle it.

stats.label: Atmosphere
stats.kids:
What is an Exosphere? On Earth, the exosphere is the outermost layer of the atmosphere (hundreds of kilometers high!), where air thins out into the vacuum of space and satellites orbit.
On Mercury, there is no lower blanket of air or sky at all—its exosphere starts right at the rocky ground! The Sun’s solar wind blasts the rocks, kicking up a tiny whisper of loose atoms (oxygen, sodium, and hydrogen) that drift into space without ever touching each other.

venus.name: Venus
venus.fact: A runaway greenhouse makes Venus the hottest planet at 465°C — hotter than Mercury despite being farther from the Sun.

kids.title: The Solar System’s Oven!
kids.jump: You jump almost identical to Earth, but the air is yellow, crushing, and hot enough to melt a tin toy car!
kids.fact: Venus spins backwards compared to Earth, so the Sun rises in the west and sets in the east.

stats.label: Distance from Sun
stats.kids: Venus is our closest neighbor planet, orbiting between Mercury and Earth. It reflects so much sunlight that it shines as the brightest object in our night sky after the Moon!

stats.label: Orbital Period
stats.kids: Venus journeys around the Sun in about 225 Earth days. Because it is closer to the Sun than Earth is, its year is about 4 months shorter than ours.

stats.label: Day Length
stats.kids: Venus spins backwards! While Earth and most planets spin counter-clockwise, Venus spins clockwise (anticlockwise from south). That means on Venus, the Sun rises in the west and sets in the east! Plus, it spins so slowly that one day on Venus is longer than its whole year!

stats.label: Equatorial Radius
stats.kids: Venus is almost the exact same size as Earth—about 95% of Earth's width! Scientists call Venus Earth’s twin sister, but she is an oven-hot, stormy twin.

stats.label: Mass
stats.kids: Venus is almost as heavy as Earth. If you stood on Venus, gravity would feel almost identical to home, pulling you down with 91% of your normal weight.

stats.label: Surface Temperature
stats.sub: Nearly 5 times hotter than boiling water — melts lead!
stats.kids: Venus is the hottest planet in the entire solar system at 465°C—nearly 5 times hotter than boiling water! Thick yellow clouds trap heat like a giant greenhouse, hot enough to melt metal like lead into puddles.

stats.label: Moons & Rings
stats.sub: Venus has no moons or natural satellites
stats.kids: Venus has 0 moons and 0 rings! Just like Mercury, any moon trying to orbit Venus would be pulled apart or stolen by the Sun’s powerful gravity.

stats.label: Atmosphere
stats.kids:
Percent (%) means parts out of 100 scoops of Venusian air:
• CO₂ (96.5 scoops) is Carbon Dioxide: the bubbly gas in soda pop that we breathe out. On Venus, it traps heat like a locked greenhouse oven!
• N₂ (3.5 scoops) is Nitrogen: the same calm gas in Earth’s sky.
There is zero O₂ (oxygen) to breathe, and yellow clouds rain real battery acid!

earth.name: Earth
earth.fact: The only known world teeming with life. Our pale blue dot is 71% ocean, wrapped in a life-giving atmosphere.

kids.title: The Just-Right Oasis!
kids.jump: Your home playground! Perfect gravity for kicking soccer goals, riding bikes, and splashing in puddles.
kids.fact: Earth is the only known planet with breathable oxygen, liquid oceans, blue skies, and living animals!

stats.label: Distance from Sun
stats.kids: Earth is in the cosmic Goldilocks Zone—just the right distance from the Sun so water stays liquid instead of boiling away or freezing solid. This distance is 1 AU (Astronomical Unit)!

stats.label: Orbital Period
stats.kids: Earth takes 365 days and 6 hours to orbit the Sun. Those extra 6 hours add up every 4 years to give us a Leap Year with an extra day on February 29!

stats.label: Day Length
stats.kids: Earth spins around once every 24 hours, giving us daytime for learning and playing and nighttime for sleeping. We spin counter-clockwise, so the Sun rises in the east and sets in the west!

stats.label: Equatorial Radius
stats.kids: Earth is the biggest of the four rocky planets! If you could dig a tunnel straight through the center from one side to the other, it would measure 12,742 kilometers.

stats.label: Mass
stats.kids: Earth weighs about 6 sextillion tons (that is a 6 followed by 24 zeros)! That mass gives us the perfect gravity to keep our oceans on the ground and air around us.

stats.label: Surface Temperature
stats.sub: Mean: 15°C — comfortable room heat with liquid oceans
stats.kids: Earth has a comfy average temperature of 15°C (room temperature)! Our atmosphere works like a cozy blanket keeping living creatures warm and happy.

stats.label: Moons & Rings
stats.sub: Earth's single natural moon is Luna (The Moon)
stats.kids: Earth has one loyal moon named Luna! The Moon causes ocean tides to rise and fall twice a day, and lights up our night sky with its gentle silver glow.

stats.label: Atmosphere
stats.kids:
What do those letters and percent numbers mean? Percent (%) means parts out of 100! Imagine a jar with 100 marbles of air:
• N₂ (78 marbles) is Nitrogen: an invisible, quiet gas that fills most of our sky and helps plants grow green and strong.
• O₂ (21 marbles) is Oxygen: the life gas that you, your family, puppies, and birds breathe in with every breath to live!
• Ar (1 marble) is Argon: a shy, peaceful gas that drifts gently without bothering anyone.
Earth’s atmosphere protects us in layers: the breathable air at the bottom, an ozone sunscreen shield in the middle, and the Exosphere at the very top (the outermost layer touching deep space where satellites orbit)!

mars.name: Mars
mars.fact: Home to Olympus Mons — the tallest volcano in the solar system at 21 km high. The rusty colour is iron-oxide dust.

kids.title: High-Jump Superhero World!
kids.jump: You jump 2.6× higher than on Earth! You could leap right over a parked car with a single bounce.
kids.fact: Mars has robot rovers like Curiosity and Perseverance rolling across red sand dunes right now.

stats.label: Distance from Sun
stats.kids: Mars is 1.5 times farther from the Sun than Earth is. Because it is farther away from the Sun’s campfire, Mars is much colder than Earth.

stats.label: Orbital Period
stats.kids: A Martian year lasts 687 Earth days—almost two Earth years! That means winter, spring, summer, and fall on Mars last twice as long as on Earth.

stats.label: Day Length
stats.kids: A day on Mars is called a "Sol", and it lasts 24 hours and 37 minutes—almost the same as an Earth day! Robot rovers on Mars go to sleep when the Martian sun sets.

stats.label: Equatorial Radius
stats.kids: Mars is about half the size of Earth. But because Mars has no oceans, its dry land area is almost the same size as all of Earth’s continents put together!

stats.label: Mass
stats.kids: Mars is only 10% as heavy as Earth. Lower weight means lower gravity: you would weigh only one-third of your Earth weight and can jump 2.6 times higher!

stats.label: Surface Temperature
stats.sub: Mean: −63°C — over 3 times colder than kitchen freezer ice
stats.kids: Mars is a freezing desert! Its average temperature is −63°C, which is over 3 times colder than kitchen freezer ice. At noon near the equator it can reach 20°C, but drops to −140°C at night.

stats.label: Moons & Rings
stats.sub: The two moons are Phobos and Deimos
stats.kids: Mars has two tiny, lumpy moons named Phobos and Deimos! They look like flying space potatoes. Phobos zips around Mars so fast that it rises in the west and sets in the east twice every day.

stats.label: Atmosphere
stats.kids:
Percent (%) means parts out of 100 scoops of thin Martian air:
• CO₂ (95 scoops) is Carbon Dioxide: the fizzy gas we exhale.
• N₂ (nearly 3 scoops) is Nitrogen.
There is almost no O₂ (oxygen) to breathe, and the air is 100 times thinner than on Earth—astronauts must always wear pressurized spacesuits with oxygen helmets!

jupiter.name: Jupiter
jupiter.fact: So massive all other planets could fit inside it. Its Great Red Spot storm has raged for over 350 years.

kids.title: King of the Heavyweights!
kids.jump: Your jumps are cut in half! Running here feels like wearing iron boots while wading through peanut butter.
kids.fact: Jupiter is so huge that 1,300 Earths fit inside it, and its Great Red Spot is a hurricane bigger than Earth!

stats.label: Distance from Sun
stats.kids: Jupiter is 5 times farther from the Sun than Earth! Out here in deep space, sunlight is 27 times dimmer and space is very cold.

stats.label: Orbital Period
stats.kids: It takes Jupiter nearly 12 Earth years to circle the Sun once! A kid would finish elementary school before celebrating their first Jupiter birthday.

stats.label: Day Length
stats.kids: Jupiter is the fastest-spinning planet in the solar system! A whole Jupiter day lasts less than 10 hours. It spins so fast that its middle bulges out like a squished ball.

stats.label: Equatorial Radius
stats.kids: Jupiter is the King of Planets—11 times wider than Earth! It is so gigantic that over 1,300 Earth globes could easily fit inside it.

stats.label: Mass
stats.kids: Jupiter is heavier than all other 7 planets put together combined, times 2.5! Its giant gravity acts like a space vacuum cleaner, pulling dangerous comets away from Earth.

stats.label: Cloud-Top Temperature
stats.sub: Cloud tops −110°C; deep core is 240 times hotter than boiling water (~24,000°C)
stats.kids: Jupiter’s cloud tops are −110°C, but deep in its core it is 24,000°C—hotter than 240 times boiling water! It gives off more heat into space than it gets from the Sun.

stats.label: Moons & Rings
stats.sub: The major moons are Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto
stats.kids: Jupiter has 95 known moons! The four biggest are Ganymede (bigger than planet Mercury!), Europa (with a huge underground ocean of warm water!), Io (with 400 active volcanoes!), and Callisto.

stats.label: Atmosphere
stats.kids:
Percent (%) means parts out of 100 scoops of Jupiter’s swirling sky:
• H₂ (90 scoops) is Hydrogen: the lightest gas in the universe, fuel for stars.
• He (10 scoops) is Helium: floaty balloon gas!
Jupiter has no solid ground to stand on—just a giant swirling ball of gas with a Great Red Spot hurricane bigger than Earth!

saturn.name: Saturn
saturn.fact: Saturn’s iconic rings span 282,000 km. It’s so low-density it would float on water!

kids.title: The Great Cosmic Bath Toy!
kids.jump: Your weight and jumps feel almost like Earth, but there is no solid ground—just fluffy gas clouds and icy rings.
kids.fact: Saturn is so light and airy that if you had a bathtub big enough, the whole planet would float like a rubber ducky!

stats.label: Distance from Sun
stats.kids: Saturn is almost 10 times farther from the Sun than Earth is! It takes sunlight about 80 minutes to travel all the way out to Saturn’s golden clouds.

stats.label: Orbital Period
stats.kids: Saturn takes 29.5 Earth years to orbit the Sun once. You would only see two or three Saturn years during your whole life on Earth!

stats.label: Day Length
stats.kids: Even though Saturn is a giant, it spins around in just 10.5 hours! This rapid spin makes Saturn wider across its middle than from top to bottom.

stats.label: Equatorial Radius
stats.kids: Saturn is 9 times wider than Earth! Including its spectacular ring system, it spans 282,000 kilometers—almost the distance from Earth all the way to the Moon!

stats.label: Mass
stats.kids: Saturn is 95 times heavier than Earth, but it is the lightest planet for its size! It is less dense than water, so if you had a gigantic bathtub, Saturn would float like a rubber ducky!

stats.label: Cloud-Top Temperature
stats.sub: Upper clouds −140°C (7 times colder than a freezer); interior is 115 times boiling water
stats.kids: Saturn’s upper clouds are −140°C (7 times colder than a freezer). But deep inside its core, it is crushed so hard that temperatures reach 11,500°C (115 times boiling water)!

stats.label: Moons & Rings
stats.sub: The major moons are Titan, Enceladus, and Mimas
stats.kids: Saturn has 146 moons—the most in the solar system! Giant moon Titan has lakes of liquid methane. Its dazzling rings are made of billions of chunks of sparkling water ice, from tiny snowflakes to house-sized icebergs!

stats.label: Atmosphere
stats.kids:
Percent (%) means parts out of 100 scoops of Saturn’s sky:
• H₂ (96 scoops) is Hydrogen: super-light star fuel.
• He (3 scoops) is Helium: party balloon gas!
Because these gases are so fluffy and light, Saturn is less dense than water and could float in a giant bathtub! Meanwhile, winds scream past at 1,800 km/h.

uranus.name: Uranus
uranus.fact: Uranus has a 98° axial tilt — it rolls around the Sun on its side. Its blue-green hue comes from methane gas.

kids.title: The Sideways Somersault World!
kids.jump: You jump 12% higher with extra bounce in your step, floating softly through frozen cyan clouds.
kids.fact: Uranus rolls on its side like a bowling ball around the Sun, and it is the coldest planet at −224°C!

stats.label: Distance from Sun
stats.kids: Uranus is 19 times farther from the Sun than Earth! It is so far away and faint that it was the first planet discovered using a telescope in 1781.

stats.label: Orbital Period
stats.kids: It takes Uranus 84 Earth years to orbit the Sun once! Because its year is so long, each season (summer, fall, winter, spring) lasts 21 Earth years.

stats.label: Day Length
stats.kids: Uranus has an extreme 98° tilt—it literally rolls on its side around the Sun like a bowling ball! Because it is tilted on its head, its spin is retrograde (anticlockwise/backwards). One pole gets 42 years of continuous sunshine, while the other pole gets 42 years of pitch-black winter!

stats.label: Equatorial Radius
stats.kids: Uranus is 4 times wider than Earth! You could line up four Earth globes side-by-side across its middle, and 63 Earths could fit inside it.

stats.label: Mass
stats.kids: Uranus is an Ice Giant planet about 14.5 times heavier than Earth. Most of its inside is a thick slush of frozen water, ammonia, and methane ices around a rocky core.

stats.label: Lowest Temperature
stats.sub: Lowest −224°C — 11 times colder than a freezer, coldest atmosphere in solar system
stats.kids: Uranus holds the record as the coldest planet in the whole solar system at −224°C! That is 11 times colder than a freezer. It has very little internal heat of its own.

stats.label: Moons & Rings
stats.sub: The major moons are Titania, Oberon, Umbriel, Ariel, and Miranda
stats.kids: Uranus has 28 known moons, all named after magical characters from William Shakespeare’s plays (like Miranda and Titania)! It also has 13 dark, charcoal-colored rings.

stats.label: Atmosphere
stats.sub: Methane absorbs red light yielding cyan hue
stats.kids:
Percent (%) means parts out of 100 scoops of chilly atmosphere:
• H₂ (82 scoops) is Hydrogen gas.
• He (15 scoops) is Helium gas (party balloon gas).
• CH₄ (over 2 scoops) is Methane gas: the same gas found in cow burps! Methane absorbs red sunlight and reflects brilliant cyan-blue light to our eyes.

neptune.name: Neptune
neptune.fact: The windiest planet — storms reach 2,100 km/h. One orbit of the Sun takes 165 Earth years.

kids.title: The Supersonic Storm Giant!
kids.jump: You feel a tiny bit heavier than Earth, like walking against the wind wearing a thick winter coat.
kids.fact: Neptune has the wildest winds in the solar system—howling past at 1,200 mph, faster than a supersonic jet!

stats.label: Distance from Sun
stats.kids: Neptune is the farthest official planet, 30 times farther from the Sun than Earth! Sunlight takes over 4 hours to reach Neptune’s dark blue clouds.

stats.label: Orbital Period
stats.kids: A year on Neptune lasts nearly 165 Earth years! Since it was discovered in 1846, Neptune has only completed one single orbit around the Sun.

stats.label: Day Length
stats.kids: Even though Neptune is a massive ice giant, it spins around once every 16 hours. Because it is made of swirling gas and slush, its equator spins faster than its poles.

stats.label: Equatorial Radius
stats.kids: Neptune is almost 4 times wider than Earth (just slightly smaller than Uranus, but heavier and denser). You could fit 57 Earths inside Neptune!

stats.label: Mass
stats.kids: Neptune is 17 times heavier than Earth! It is packed with a deep ocean of compressed hot water, ammonia, and methane slush over a rocky iron core.

stats.label: Cloud-Top Temperature
stats.sub: Mean −201°C — 10 times colder than a freezer, freezes nitrogen gas
stats.kids: Neptune’s cloud tops are −201°C, which is 10 times colder than a kitchen freezer. It is so cold that nitrogen gas freezes into solid snow crystals!

stats.label: Moons & Rings
stats.sub: The major moons are Triton, Proteus, and Nereid
stats.kids: Neptune has 16 moons, led by giant icy Triton. Triton is extraordinary: it orbits backwards (anticlockwise/retrograde) in the opposite direction of Neptune’s spin! That proves Triton was an icy dwarf planet captured from the Kuiper Belt! Triton even shoots real nitrogen ice volcanoes into space.

stats.label: Atmosphere
stats.sub: Vivid azure blue with Great Dark Spot
stats.kids:
Percent (%) means parts out of 100 scoops of icy atmosphere:
• H₂ (80 scoops) is Hydrogen gas.
• He (19 scoops) is Helium gas (party balloon gas).
• CH₄ (1.5 scoops) is Methane gas: this magical gas swallows red sunlight and reflects deep, gorgeous ocean-blue light!
Wild storms whip through this blue gas at over 2,100 km/h!

luna.name: Luna (The Moon)
luna.fact: Earth's only natural satellite. Tidally locked in synchronous rotation, Luna controls Earth's ocean tides and is the only other world humans have walked upon.

kids.title: Super-Bouncing Lunar Playground!
kids.jump: You jump 6× higher than on Earth! A single bounce can launch you over a two-story house.
kids.fact: Apollo astronaut footprints in the lunar dust will last for millions of years because there is no wind or rain to erase them!

stats.label: Distance from Earth
stats.kids: The Moon is 384,400 km from Earth. That is far enough that all other 7 planets in our solar system could fit side-by-side in between Earth and the Moon!

stats.label: Orbital Period
stats.kids: The Moon takes 27.3 days to orbit around Earth. Because it spins at the exact same rate as it orbits, we always see the same face of the Moon from Earth!

stats.label: Day Length
stats.kids: A full day on the Moon lasts nearly 30 Earth days! That means two weeks of blazing sunshine followed by two weeks of freezing, star-filled night.

stats.label: Equatorial Radius
stats.kids: The Moon is more than a quarter the width of Earth. If Earth were the size of a basketball, the Moon would be the size of a tennis ball!

stats.label: Mass
stats.kids: The Moon has only about 1.2% of Earth's mass. Lower mass means lower gravity: you weigh only 1/6th of your Earth weight and feel like a flying superhero!

stats.label: Surface Temperature
stats.kids: Without an atmosphere to trap heat, the Moon swings from 120°C in direct sunlight down to −130°C in dark shadows. Spacesuits keep astronauts at a comfortable room temperature.

stats.label: Moons & Rings
stats.kids: The Moon has no moons of its own! Instead, it is Earth's loyal companion, creating our ocean tides twice every day.

stats.label: Atmosphere
stats.sub: Trace He, Ne, H₂, Ar (< 10⁻¹⁰ Pa)
stats.kids: The Moon has no breathable air—it is a silent vacuum. Sound needs air to travel, so astronauts must talk to each other using radios inside their helmets!

game.quiz_q_moon: Can you hear loud sounds on the Moon?
game.quiz_hint_moon: Sound needs air waves to travel, and the Moon has almost no atmosphere.
game.quiz_q_mars: Why does Mars look reddish-orange in the sky?
game.quiz_hint_mars: The Martian rocks and soil are loaded with iron oxide—the same ingredient in rust!
game.quiz_q_jupiter: What is Jupiter's famous Great Red Spot?
game.quiz_hint_jupiter: It is a massive high-pressure storm larger than the entire planet Earth!
game.quiz_q_saturn: What are Saturn's rings mostly made of?

game.quiz_q_neptune: Why does Neptune look like a brilliant blue marble?
game.quiz_hint_neptune: Methane gas absorbs red light and reflects deep azure blue light back into space!
game.quiz_q_earth: Why is Earth the only known planet full of life?
game.quiz_hint_earth: Earth sits in the habitable zone where liquid water, oxygen, and moderate temperatures thrive!

game.riddle_adv_earth: Deep Space Riddle: Launch to the only known haven in the cosmos with oceans and life!

game.quiz_q_venus: Why is Venus hotter than Mercury even though it is farther from the Sun?

game.grand_tour_completed_desc: Congratulations, Commander! You navigated the entire Solar System and safely touched down on Earth! You earned +250 Cosmic Stars ⭐. Deep Space Expeditions are now unlocked for infinite exploration!
game.freeplay_clue: Choose any planet, adjust thrust energy, and launch! On touchdown, you will explore full scientific briefing and planetary stats.
game.future_rendezvous_principle: 🚀 Keplerian Rendezvous: Planets orbit continuously while you fly! You must aim for where the planet will be upon arrival (T+{sec}s), not where it is today.
game.planner_subtitle: Planets advance along orbits over time. Preview future orbital alignments to pick optimal transfer windows.
game.tap_planet_map_hint: Tap any planet on map to target!
game.select_target_prompt: Select on Map or tap Luna
game.debrief_perigee_desc: The orbital point where origin and destination planets are closest together. Launching near Perigee requires minimum thrust (delta-v) and fuel for orbital capture.
game.debrief_apogee_desc: The orbital point of maximum separation. In your trajectory, Apogee is the peak altitude your rocket reaches before falling back toward the Sun.
game.debrief_why_matters_fuel: Your thrust was too low ({thrust}%), so your orbit's apogee fell short of the target planet. Increase thrust into the green window or wait for Perigee!
game.debrief_why_matters_overshoot: Your thrust was too high ({thrust}%), blasting your apogee beyond planetary gravity into deep space. Dial back into the green window.
game.debrief_why_matters_general: Orbits are ellipses, not straight lines! To rendezvous with a planet, your trajectory's apogee must intersect the target's orbit at the exact arrival time.
